articles.title_orig: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
articles.title_zh: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
articles.content_orig:
Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June.
Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care.
“Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release .
Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million.
Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership.
Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports.
“At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.”
The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.
Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth.
The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

articles.title_orig: Chip stocks' slide nears $5 trillion as Nvidia hits most extreme selling level since 2019
articles.title_zh: Chip stocks' slide nears $5 trillion as Nvidia hits most extreme selling level since 2019
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
It took five minutes for Tuesday's hot inflation report to knock stocks lower, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) never recovered. The chipmaker hasn't been sold this hard, this fast since 2019, but the typical S&P 500 stock finished the day flat.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) closed down about 0.4% Tuesday after an afternoon rebound, shedding about $250 billion in market value according to Yahoo Finance calculations. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) also fell about 0.4%, while the equal-weight S&P 500 ( RSP ), which gives every company the same weight, finished flat.
Nvidia closed down about 6%, as the scandal surrounding CEO Jensen Huang drags on. Its relative strength index , a gauge of how fast and how far a stock has moved, sank to 24 out of a possible 100 — its most oversold reading since June 2019.
Read more: Nvidia stock drops as spy fiasco involving CEO Jensen Huang raises broader risk concerns
Memory makers Micron ( MU ) and SanDisk ( SNDK ) and chip designer Arm ( ARM ) fell roughly 1% to 3%. AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) rose, adding to Monday's surge.
The longer view is starker. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks has lost nearly $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, roughly a quarter of its worth. That's more than the roughly $2.7 trillion the entire S&P 500 has shed over the same stretch, even though the basket includes some companies outside the index.
Tuesday's trigger was a hotter-than-expected October consumer price index . S&P 500 futures fell about 0.5% in the five minutes after the 8:30 a.m. ET release, on volume many times the morning's norm. Nasdaq 100 futures briefly erased their losses by 10 a.m., slid again, then recovered much of the damage in the afternoon.
Bonds felt it too. The 5-year Treasury yield ( ^FVX ) posted its biggest one-day jump since September, and the 10-year ( ^TNX ) briefly topped 5% as traders raised bets on a December rate hike .
BofA's Savita Subramanian sees the bigger risk in the S&P 500 itself.
"We're not particularly bullish on the index. I think the index itself is a bit risky," the head of US equity and quantitative strategy at BofA Securities told Yahoo Finance on Tuesday. "What's the most crowded equity ticker in the world? It's the S&P index."
The typical stock looks nothing like the index. The equal-weighted S&P 500 is up about 4% since Oct. 6 and closed at a record on Nov. 4.
Some see Nvidia's slide as a chance to buy. "I think if [CEO Jensen Huang] stays, then this is going to prove to be overdone. And you know this will be a strong buying opportunity," Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon said Monday on Yahoo Finance's "Deirdre Bosa Live."
Veteran trader Michael Martin isn't convinced . "I don't think these are buying opportunities. Everything is in a downtrend," he told Yahoo Finance on Friday.
The Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) turned lower Monday right at its 200-day moving average , and the Cboe Volatility Index ( ^VIX ) topped 21 Tuesday before settling back below 20, a level associated with expectations of higher-than-average volatility over the next month.
Nvidia reports quarterly results after the bell on Nov. 17, and Anthropic's IPO could follow as soon as Nov. 19.
Subramanian isn't giving up on the AI trade. "I think you want to stay long," she said. "The idea that AI is not the metaverse. It's going to continue."

The swift downfall of “one of Wall Street’s most vaunted law firms” last week has put the legal industry on edge, said Erin Mulvaney and Andrew Scurria in The Wall Street Journal . Weil, Gotshal & Manges—a fixture among corporate dealmakers for nearly a century—was “one of the 20 most profitable in the business,” raking in $2.1 billion in revenue last year with “relatively few liabilities,” apart from a lease on a roughly 380,000-square-foot office on Fifth Avenue in New York City. What it didn’t have was loyalty. The firm has “hemorrhaged top lawyers” in recent months after rivals poached top partners, including private-equity attorney Ramona Nee, who was chosen to lead the firm in 2027. In September, Weil’s “top dealmaker,” Michael Aiello, left too, and “confidence in Weil’s future cratered” in a matter of weeks. “A law firm’s most valuable asset is its people,” said bankruptcy attorney Albert Togut. “If they go home one night and don’t come back the next day, it’s over.”
This is the “logical consequence of an industry engaging in a Darwinian war for talent,” said Chris Bryant in Bloomberg . Some legal superstars today are making up to $40 million a year, an impossible figure for most small or even midsize firms to match. “Big Law has moved away from paying counsel according to seniority”—which incentivized allegiance—“and has oriented more toward an individual’s results.” It’s created an “eat-what-you-kill” attitude that has made the entire legal industry unstable. Rivals “shouldn’t kid themselves” if they think “the same couldn’t happen to them.”
It also didn’t help that Weil “botched” its succession plan, said Diane Brady in Fortune . The choice of Nee was made unconventionally, without much partner input, and “there was no plan B” when she announced in September that she “no longer planned to take the role.” That’s one of the “lessons” that other CEOs should heed from this “sad narrative.”

The legal industry looks strong today on the surface, said Sara Randazzo in Reuters , but it is “astonishingly fragile.” Unlike corporate executives , partners aren’t “sitting on stock options that give them a powerful financial incentive to stay.” Even a slight “loss of confidence in a firm’s direction can be enough to set off a rush for the exits.”
The partnership structure, “once an instrument of stability, is now a liability” when your talent prefers to think of themselves as “the world’s best-paid gig workers,” said The Economist . How can order be restored? Noncompete agreements have “never been used by law firms” in the U.S., but they are customary in the U.K. and on Wall Street. “The legal industry’s Lehman moment” might require a drastic change to how law firms do business.

articles.title_zh: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
articles.content_orig:
Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.
This Patch Tuesday addresses 66 "Critical" vulnerabilities, 48 of which are Remote Code Execution (RCE), 15 are Elevation of Privilege (EoP), and three are Use-After-Free in Microsoft Edge.
The approximate number of bugs in each vulnerability category is listed below:
Of the 1,235 vulnerabilities, approximately 639 are categorized under Windows or Microsoft Windows products/components.
When BleepingComputer reports on Patch Tuesday security updates, we only count vulnerabilities released by Microsoft on Patch Tuesday itself.
Therefore, today's total excludes 108 flaws fixed earlier this month, including one Entra Device Registration, 82 Mariner, and 25 Microsoft Edge flaws.
November's Patch Tuesday comes after a record-breaking 1,411 flaws in the October updates as Microsoft continues to use AI to find and patch vulnerabilities.
To learn more about the non-security updates released today, you can review our dedicated articles on the Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates and the Microsoft Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update .
This month's Patch Tuesday fixes one zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook that was exploited in attacks.
Microsoft classifies a zero-day flaw as publicly disclosed or actively exploited when no official fix is available.
The actively exploited zero-day vulnerability addressed in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates is:
CVE-2026-124194 - Microsoft Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability
Microsoft patched a Microsoft Outlook Spoofing zero-day vulnerability that was actively exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.
"An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook," warns Microsoft.
"Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction."
This type of vulnerability is known as an NTLM credential disclosure flaw, where a malicious attachment, when opened, causes Windows to connect to an attacker-controlled network share.
When connecting, Windows may automatically attempt to authenticate to the remote server, exposing the user's NTLMv2 authentication hash, which can then be captured by the attacker and potentially cracked offline.
The recovered credentials could then be used to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts.
Similar vulnerability have been exploited in the past , typically through malicious attachments sent in phishing campaigns .

articles.title_orig: Eisenkot unveils agenda to reverse Netanyahu’s policies as Israel's new parliament is sworn in
articles.title_zh: Eisenkot unveils agenda to reverse Netanyahu’s policies as Israel's new parliament is sworn in
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in his address to the Knesset on Tuesday that Iran is working to renew its nuclear threat, and that "the only way to permanently remove this existential threat is through the downfall of the Ayatollah regime."
Netanyahu also warned that Israel will imminently face international pressure to accept Iran as a nuclear power and "to tolerate the terrifying regime seeking its destruction."
He also added that Israel can be expected to be pressured to "retreat from its monumental achievements and from the major progress made regarding security zones."
The IDF assessed that Iran's nuclear capabilities were severely damaged by strikes during the recent war, though Tehran maintains the capacity to achieve nuclear weapons in approximately one to two years.
The prime minister then pushed for Knesset members to set aside other priorities and considerations in order to form a national unity government, insisting that only such a government is capable of facing such challenges.
Netanyahu's speech was interrupted by former prime minister and B'Yachad MK Naftali Bennett , who shouted at him, "What about your Qatari advisers? What about investigating October 7?"
Bennett's remarks drew an inaudible response from Netanyahu's wife, Sara, and son, Yair, who were in attendance.
Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party, called the speech "delusional, divisive, hate-filled, and shameful," and accused Netanyahu of abusing his platform at the 26th Knesset swear-in.
Eisenkot added that the address further convinced him that the prime minister must be replaced and is "unfit to remain in office for even one more minute."
He urged the Knesset to establish a national emergency government, claiming that Netanyahu's rule jeopardizes the security of the state.

articles.content_orig:
Claim your business, keep your information current, and understand how people engage with you in ChatGPT
We’re introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving businesses a new way to connect with the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. Through Business Hub ⁠ (opens in a new window) , businesses can claim their business, manage their information, and see insights on how people engage with them on ChatGPT. In addition, we are adding a powerful new way for businesses to interact with users via Business Agents, starting with eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the U.S.
Together, these products create more ways for businesses to connect with people as they explore options and make decisions. They strengthen how people discover and interact with businesses in ChatGPT through broader business coverage, up-to-date information, and the ability to connect with a business through its Business Agent. Throughout these experiences, protecting the trust people place in ChatGPT remains our North Star.
In Business Hub, companies can claim their organization in ChatGPT and, once verified, update key details and add self-service product feeds with pricing and availability. This gives businesses a new way to provide information to ChatGPT, helping people explore products and services using the most accurate and up-to-date details.
Any eligible business located where ChatGPT is available can claim their business in ChatGPT through Business Hub. Existing OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers can work directly with their OpenAI representative to claim their business. Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin to streamline verification. Eligible products from Shopify merchants are already integrated into ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog.
Business Hub provides aggregated insights into how people engage with a business in ChatGPT. This includes the number of mentions and website clicks a business receives. Businesses can also explore discovery topics—common themes across conversations where their website is cited. These insights can help businesses understand how they’re represented and find opportunities to improve the information they share.
We’ve designed these insights to protect user privacy. We don’t share users’ conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses. Insights are aggregated and are only available when there are enough conversations or interactions to meet certain thresholds.
After claiming their business in ChatGPT, eligible organizations can build, test, and launch a Business Agent—a new way to answer questions and help people explore their offerings.
When a business appears in a model response, people can click to see the business’s ChatGPT profile. If a Business Agent is available, customers can choose to start a conversation with the business to explore its offerings and ask follow-up questions. For example, someone comparing products could ask about the differences between two options and which features fit their needs. A Business Agent could help them explore those questions using the business’s information.
For customers, this can make it easier to understand whether an offering is the right fit. For businesses, it creates a way to help interested customers learn more through a personalized conversation. The Business Agent conversation is clearly labeled, separate from the customer’s original ChatGPT conversation, and distinct from ChatGPT’s independent answers.
Businesses can also sponsor their Business Agent ⁠ and use it as the destination for ChatGPT Ads to reach more potential customers. Sponsored placements are clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT responses.
Business Agents are now available to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States . Learn more about eligible categories here ⁠ .
As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI. Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT. We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights, and conversations that help people make informed decisions. Over time, we plan to expand Businesses in ChatGPT and Business Agents to more markets and business categories, and build tools for organizations with more complex needs.
As the platform evolves, we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers—directly or through agents—in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.
Learn more and ⁠ claim your business in ChatGPT. ⁠

articles.title_orig: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
articles.title_zh: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
articles.content_orig:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) told makers of popular weight-loss GLP-1 drugs that they must add warning labels about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness.
Manufacturers of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound must warn about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). The disorder happens when vessels supplying blood to the optic nerves become blocked, depriving the nerves of oxygen.
The condition can cause painless decreased vision in one eye, which can be permanent, the FDA said.
In a statement to the BBC, the American Academy of Ophthalmology said "any added risk appears small, and it has not been established that these medications cause NAION".
"GLP-1 medications offer important benefits for people with diabetes, obesity, and heart disease, so our message to patients is simple," the group said. "Don't stop your medication without talking to your doctor, and if you notice sudden, painless vision loss in one eye, see an ophthalmologist promptly."
There is no known treatment to reverse vision loss caused by NAION. It is the most common cause of acute optic nerve injury in people over 50 years old, according to the academy.
The FDA said it conducted a detailed review of reports of NAION in GLP-1 users as well as a review of other studies and concluded there is an "increased risk of rare NAION events" in people taking the drugs.
In a statement, Novo Nordisk, the manufacturer of Wegovy, one of the most popular weight-loss medications, said the company believes the data "do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship".
"We recognize that NAION can have a profound impact on patients and their families. Patient safety is a top priority for Novo, and we continue to monitor the safety of our medicines," the manufacturer said.
Some research was challenging to review because people taking GLP-1 drugs for obesity and type 2 diabetes may already have risk factors for NAION separate from the drugs, according to the regulator. The FDA said it was not known why those taking GLP-1 drugs may be more at risk for the eye condition.
The drugs already have warning labels for several other conditions including pancreatitis and gallbladder disease. Some of the most common symptoms for semaglutide - a key ingredient in many GLP-1 drugs - include nausea, vomiting and stomach pain.
â Last year, a safety arm of the European Medicines Agency, a part of the European Union, said up to 1 in 10,000 people taking semaglutide may be affected by NAION.
In a study published two years ago analysing 17,000 patients, US researchers found those taking semaglutide were four times more likely to be diagnosed with NAION than those not taking the drug.
But one of the authors of the study, Harvard Medical School ophthalmology professor Dr Joseph Rizzo, said the findings were "significant but tentative", and  more research was needed on the relationship between the drug and the eye condition in a more diverse population.

articles.title_orig: Amazon's Ring launches flying security drones, patrol robots to guard homes, businesses
articles.title_zh: Amazon's Ring launches flying security drones, patrol robots to guard homes, businesses
articles.content_orig:
Amazon 's Ring is going deeper into surveillance with an indoor drone for home monitoring and an autonomous robot designed to patrol businesses.
The company on Tuesday unveiled the $250 Ring Drone Cam, a security camera that can fly from room to room, including upstairs, as well as capture footage during the day or at night. When an alarm or sensor on windows, doors and home security devices is triggered, the textbook-sized drone travels a preset path to investigate suspicious activity. Users can also deploy the drone at any time, the company said.
At a demo in New York on Monday, Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff said the drone could be used as a home monitoring tool and as a crime "deterrent" due to the device's built-in LED lights.
"If someone is going around your house at night, and your motion detector goes off on your Ring doorbell, imagine if you see spotlights and something flying across the window," Siminoff said. "You're probably not going to go into that house."
The drone, which can fly up to eight minutes at a time before autonomously returning to its charging dock, has two plastic-encased propellers that emit a loud buzz when it's airborne.
Ring devices have provided Amazon another avenue to grow its presence in the smart home beyond its Echo smart speakers and Eero routers, expanding in a market that Grand View Research estimates will top $200 billion in sales this year. It's equally fertile ground for Amazon rivals Apple and Google .
Ring, which Amazon acquired in 2018 and is known for its doorbells, has been beset with privacy concerns , primarily due to its partnerships with police. Earlier this year, Ring faced renewed scrutiny over a controversial Super Bowl ad touting an AI pet-finding tool called "Search Party." It then canceled an integration with police tech provider Flock Safety , which has also faced widespread backlash over its automated license plate readers.
Ring first previewed its drone, then called the Always Home Cam , in 2020. Siminoff said he chose to hold off on releasing the device until Amazon could perfect the design, sensors and data processing.
The company on Tuesday also debuted the $1,000 Ring Rover Cam. The device repurposes Amazon's Astro home robot , which had a short life as a business device and has seen few upgrades since its 2021 debut, for companies to use to patrol offices, warehouses and other workspaces.
Ring said it "leveraged the best of Astro" to build the Ring Rover Cam, which it describes as a "purpose-built security robot."
Similar to the Astro, the device is a display mounted on a two-wheeled base with an extendable periscope camera. It also features a "built-in siren," two-way audio and a "light tower" that shines onto the ceiling to help users keep track of its whereabouts.
Siminoff said in an interview that the drone and the robot allow users to monitor multiple areas of their home or business with just one device.
"People like indoor cameras, but they don't necessarily want them everywhere around their home," Siminoff said.
Ring said privacy is the "default" mode for both the drone and the robot, which flash an LED light when they're recording.
Siminoff said the drone can't fly outside per Federal Aviation Administration regulations, which restrict operating drones unless they're within a line of sight of a pilot.
"We have told our customers not to do that because it's illegal," Siminoff said. "We've also put guardrails in there to make it so it doesn't fly outside."
The Ring Drone Cam ships in the U.S. on Jan. 27, pending approval from the Federal Communications Commission, while the Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping to users on Dec. 16, the company said.

Windows 11 is getting another substantial batch of changes in November, but after going through what's coming, two improvements stand out to me: the customizable context menu and Cloud Rebuild.
The first finally gives you control over some of the clutter that has plagued Windows 11's right-click menu, while Cloud Rebuild offers a much easier way to reinstall Windows without creating a bootable USB drive.
Those are only two of the 11 changes worth knowing about this month , which also include improvements for handheld gaming, Phone Link , accessibility , Edge performance, security, and more.
Availability will vary because Microsoft rolls many features out gradually , but here's what you should be watching for in our latest Windows 11 guide .
Here's all you need to know about the features and changes coming in November.
Starting with the November update, Windows 11 is getting a new context menu experience that gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear in the main menu.
The new menu reduces clutter and makes the experience faster by moving app extensions into a separate submenu. It also introduces a "Customize menu" option at the bottom of the interface, which opens a dedicated Settings page where you can enable or disable built-in commands, add options such as "Print" and "Send to," and control which app extensions appear in the main menu or submenu.
You can also display "Cut," "Copy," "Paste," "Rename," "Delete," and "Share" as individual commands instead of showing them in a vertical view. Windows 11 also lets you move "Properties" to the bottom of the menu as it appeared on Windows 10 .
To access these options, right-click a file, folder, or the desktop and select Customize menu , or open Settings > Personalization > Context menu .
You can keep the default configuration if you prefer. Holding down "Shift" while right-clicking also reveals the legacy context menu.
The ability to customize the menu is particularly useful because it gives users more control over which commands they see without forcing everyone to use the same layout.
Microsoft is also refreshing the Gaming Task View experience in XBOX mode. The updated interface retains the familiar design but adds a navigation bar that makes it easier to access options such as "Exit to Desktop" and "Power Options" using a game controller.
It's a relatively small change, but it makes basic actions easier to navigate using a gaming controller.
The Settings app is getting a few usability refinements. The "Privacy & security" page now groups Location, Microphone, and Camera controls more clearly, making it easier to review these permissions.
Microsoft is also expanding the "Device Info" card on the "Home" page to more markets. Available to users signed in with a Microsoft account, the card provides an overview of key hardware specifications and a shortcut to the "About" page.
The "Storage" page is also getting visual changes to its temporary files section.
These aren't major additions, but they make some commonly used Settings pages easier to navigate.
Phone Link integration is getting a small convenience improvement. When your phone is connected, you can hover over a recent message or notification in the Start menu 's "Recent" section of the mobile pane to preview its contents without opening it.
It's a minor addition, but it makes checking incoming messages more convenient without opening your phone or the Phone Link app.
The Magnifier feature is getting three useful improvements, including independent zoom levels for multiple monitors, viewport locking, and a new contrast theme. These additions give you more control over magnified content while making it easier to work across multiple displays.
The biggest improvement is per-monitor zoom, which lets you assign a different magnification level to each display. For example, you can keep one monitor at 150 percent and another at 200 percent.
The feature is enabled by default, but displays must use "Extend" mode. Adjust each screen with the Magnifier toolbar or shortcuts (" Windows key + Plus/Minus "). Viewport locking keeps one magnified screen fixed while you move the pointer to another. Use " Ctrl + Windows key + K " to lock/unlock or " Windows key + Esc " to release all. A new dark contrast theme reduces glare while keeping colors intact. Enable it from the Magnifier toolbar or Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier. Color inversion is separate.
The Narrator feature now supports reading and navigating math equations, making it easier for people with low vision to understand formulas, equations, and scientific notation.
The feature works with supported Microsoft 365 apps, including Word and PowerPoint, as well as web content in Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome .
You can use it with the "Narrator key + Alt + N" shortcut to enable math navigation, and then use the arrow keys to explore individual parts of an equation. Use the "Esc" key to exit. Math reading supports six languages, including English, German, Spanish, Finnish, and Traditional Chinese.
You can change the language and other preferences under Settings > Accessibility > Narrator > Math reading .
Browser support requires Microsoft Edge version 153.0.4234.32 or later, or Google Chrome version 153.0.8010.18 or later.
Windows 11 is making recovery easier by allowing the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles saved in the main operating system.
This allows computers to connect automatically to supported wireless networks during recovery operations such as Quick Machine Recovery and Cloud Rebuild, without requiring administrators to configure Wi-Fi credentials separately during recovery.
The feature is enabled by default and supports certain certificate-based enterprise networks, though it doesn't currently support TPM-backed certificate keys. Network administrators can turn off the capability through the Recovery Configuration Service Provider (CSP) .
WinRE only accesses saved network credentials when a recovery operation requires connectivity, rather than maintaining a permanent network connection.
I've been testing Cloud Rebuild , and eliminating the need to create installation media is easily its biggest advantage. However, I also ran into an important limitation: the feature depends on Windows Update having the drivers your PC needs.
Unlike a traditional local reinstall, it doesn't depend on the existing Windows installation or require a bootable USB drive or a custom recovery image. You can also start it from the Windows Recovery Environment when the device cannot boot.
You can start the process under Settings > System > Recovery and use the "Rebuild this PC" option, or from WinRE by selecting Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud Rebuild . After connecting to Ethernet or Wi-Fi, the system will display the target build, edition, and language before installation.
The feature includes two options to clean the drive. For example, the "Remove files" option reformats the system drive, although specialized recovery tools might still recover some data. On the other hand, the "Remove and sanitize files" option uses the storage hardware's erase capability to eras

articles.title_zh: Greta Thunberg warns ‘everything we love is at stake’ as she arrives at UN climate talks
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in

Prominent climate change activist Greta Thunberg arrived Tuesday at the U.N. climate meeting, where she emphasized the need to protect people and the planet over profits and power.
This year's meeting — called the Conference of the Parties, or COP31 — comes after a year of climate-induced heat waves and other disasters.
As she arrived at the meeting venue in Antalya , Turkey, Thunberg said climate change is “threatening everything" and that “everything and everyone we love is at stake.”
“We should act to protect and benefit people rather than constantly sacrificing the global majority and the very planet we are all living on, for a fortunate few to keep making unimaginable profits and maintaining geopolitical power,” she told reporters.
Thunberg is attending her first U.N. climate summit since she participated in the 2021 COP in Glasgow , Scotland , where she dismissed promises made by global leaders as “blah, blah, blah."
In 2024, Thunberg participated in a protest rally in Georgia against Azerbaijan hosting that year's climate talks. Thunberg accused Azerbaijan of using that summit to "greenwash their crimes and human rights abuses.”
Thunberg is expected to join this year's talks for a few days. She said structural changes are needed across the world to deal with the climate crisis because current political and economic systems “have become incompatible with human nature.”
Arasu reported from Bengaluru, India.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 One-Shots a Playable FPS Game in Just 8 Hours
articles.title_zh: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 One-Shots a Playable FPS Game in Just 8 Hours
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 represents a significant development in AI modeling, demonstrating its capacity to tackle complex and resource-intensive tasks. For example, it successfully created a fully playable Gears of War-style game with advanced mechanics, though the project required up to 12 billion tokens and incurred an estimated $15,000 in API costs. These results suggest that Fable 5.2 is particularly suited for high-budget applications, according to Matthew Berman.
Discover how Fable 5.2 performs in game development, including its ability to produce AAA-level projects like Tumble Beans. Gain insight into its capacity to replicate productivity software, such as a browser-based Excel alternative, and its engineering achievements, including the creation of a 3D printable tower designed to meet strict specifications. This guide examines the model’s strengths, challenges, and practical applications for demanding scenarios.
Fable 5.2 , Anthropic’s latest AI model, has been noted for its exceptional power and versatility. Testing highlighted its ability to perform across diverse applications, including game development and architectural rendering. However, its high performance comes with a premium cost, making it suitable for demanding, resource-intensive use cases.
Fable 5.2 demonstrated its capabilities in game development with a fully playable Gears of War clone . Built using Ultra Code mode, the game featured advanced lighting, textures, and mechanics like barrier-based cover, timed reloads, and full battles. Focused on a single level, the project consumed 8-12 billion tokens at an estimated API cost of $15,000. Despite a minor animation flaw, the game was described as “fun to play” and executed the requested level flawlessly.
Another notable project was Tumble Beans , a multiplayer game inspired by Fall Guys. It included 10 uniquely designed levels and realistic physics, requiring over 9 billion tokens, 71 hours of build time, and an estimated cost of $13,000. The result was a polished, enjoyable experience with monetization potential.
Additional projects included a Call of Duty-style multiplayer game with block-style graphics, a Portal clone with functional but subpar visuals, and Dragon Rider , which featured high-quality graphics. Starlane, similar to F-Zero, stood out for its visuals, while Tidekeeper, a sequel to a previous game, introduced a crab as the main control element. All narration in these games was AI-generated.
The model also created a large-scale 3D visualization of Tokyo, complete with traffic, pedestrians, trains, and ray-traced reflections. Every building was constructed from scratch by a new cloud model. This project used 6.72 billion tokens, took about 70 hours, and cost an estimated $11,000.
Explore further guides and articles from our vast library that you may find relevant to your interests in Fable.
Fable 5.2 excelled in replicating complex productivity software. A browser-based Excel clone was described as “literally perfect,” offering features like formulas, pivot tables, and an example sales tracker. This project required 50 hours, 8 billion input tokens, and 15 million output tokens, costing approximately $11,700.
Similarly, a Da Vinci Resolve clone included essential features such as waveform and video displays, clip splitting, and magnetic snapping. Another video editor, Kestrel, developed for Windows PCs, offered keyboard shortcuts, zoom functionality, and keyframe insertion. Unlike the browser-based tools, Kestrel could potentially be adapted for Mac or web use. Both tools were noted for their flawless functionality.
The model’s versatility extended to creative and technical projects. A 3D simulation of a bullet piercing a water-filled balloon was coded entirely from scratch, without external libraries or dependencies. Users could adjust parameters like bullet speed, caliber, lighting, gravity, and balloon size in real time, with physics recalculated instantly. The project, which included a 9 mm bullet as an example, took 2.5 hours and cost $91 for 41 million tokens.
In Blender, the model rendered a detailed house with a pool, solar panels, and realistic lighting. The project used 13 million tokens and cost $30. While visually impressive, minor errors, such as a tree placed in the driveway, were noted.
Motion graphics for technical explanations were also produced, including visualizations of software decompiling and LLM training processes. The software decompiling project, completed in 45 minutes using 9.5 million tokens at a cost of $25, delivered high-quality visuals for complex topics.
Fable 5.2 demonstrated engineering capabilities by designing a 3D printable tower that met specific constraints. Using a Bamboo Lab P2S printer with a 4 mm nozzle and PLA filament, the tower weighed under 10 g and withstood significant weight before collapsing. The design process took just over an hour, used 10 million tokens, and cost $37.
Benchmark testing validated the model’s performance. It achieved an 89.3 on OSWorld 2.1 , surpassing Astra at 79.5 and Opus 5.5 at 87. Other scores included 74.6 on Terminal Bench Science and 74.2 on Humanity’s Last Exam, nearly 10 points higher than Fable 5.1. On the Frontier SWE benchmark, it scored 69.9, outperforming all other models, including Opus 5.5. However, it scored 51 on the Automation Bench benchmark, falling short of Carbon’s 53.
Fable 5.2 also demonstrated remarkable speed and autonomy. Tasks that previously took 60-120 minutes with Ultra Code now required a maximum of 10 minutes. It made correct decisions nine times out of 10, significantly improving workflows. During a full code review using Max Thinking effort and Ultra Code, it identified numerous bugs, security issues, and UI inconsistencies.
Fable 5.2’s pricing reflects its capabilities. The model costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, a 20% reduction from Fable 5.1. Fast mode, offering 2.5 times the speed, costs $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens, though it was not available for testing. Fable resets depend on subscription status, account access, and subscription duration.
While Fable 5.2 outperformed Opus 5.5 in speed and capability, Opus 5.5 remains more efficient and cost-effective. Ultra Code mode, though powerful, is extremely expensive and unsuitable for most users. Recreations of real-world events, such as the Roadster launch, were less impressive, highlighting occasional limitations in specific contexts.
On balance, Fable 5.2 represents a significant leap in AI capabilities, particularly for high-budget, high-complexity projects. However, its cost and occasional limitations may restrict its accessibility for smaller-scale applications.

articles.title_zh: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of women have come forward with abuse allegations against the former Harrods and Ritz Paris owner
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-ThÃ©rÃ¨se in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
The Ritz hotel in Paris is still owned by the Al Fayed family
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: Anti-gay laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.title_zh: Anti-gay laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.content_orig:
A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago.
London's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC), the Caribbean island's final court of appeal, ruled the laws were not in keeping with the "fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life."
The judgement is the result of an 11-year legal battle brought by dual-citizen Jason Jones, 62, who said he hoped it would "accelerate the fight for full equality."
Jones had successfully challenged the laws in 2018 in Trinidad's High Court, however the ruling was overturned on appeal by the Trinidadian government.
It is the first time the JCPC has ever decided on a case to decriminalise same-sex intimacy, and campaigners hope it will spark similar successful legal challenges elsewhere in the Commonwealth.
Prior to this historic decision, Trinidad and Tobago was one of some 34 Commonwealth countries continuing to criminalise homosexuality based on colonial-era British laws.
Under these laws, consensual same-sex intimacy is punishable by imprisonment, and in some cases carries the death penalty.
The Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago had argued that the law was protected from legal challenges by the "savings law clauses" - which carried over existing British laws into newly independent states.
Representatives for Jones argued that the laws violated an individual's right to privacy and argued the government's changes to the laws in 1986 - which saw stricter punishments introduced - meant the savings clause protections no longer applied.
The judicial committee unanimously found in favour of Jones.
Handing down the judgement, Lord Sales told the court the laws "cannot be regarded as reasonably justifiable in a society that has a proper respect for the rights and freedoms of an individual".
Jones, human rights campaigner and appellant in the appeal, said: "These laws never reflected who we are as a people and a nation - diverse, multiracial, and secular.
"They told LGBTQ+ people that we were criminals in our own country. That message ends today."
Lawyer Anand Ramlogan SC, representing Jones, said the judgement was a "landmark victory for gay rights, equal dignity and respect for private and family life in Trinidad and Tobago."

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Is Down 30% From Its High. History Says This Is What Happens Next.
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Is Down 30% From Its High. History Says This Is What Happens Next.
articles.content_orig:
From the all-time high it hit about a month ago, Nvidia ( NVDA -5.47% ) has lost 30% of its value, and has lost its status as the most valuable company in the world.
This isn't the first time Nvidia stock has plummeted. Based on how it has performed historically, here's what is likely to happen next.
It's hard to believe that just four years ago, Nvidia was a relatively obscure tech company making graphics processing units (GPUs) primarily for the video game and crypto-mining markets. But when the generative artificial intelligence (AI) revolution arrived, it had the proprietary technology to power that software ready and waiting, and it has provided the foundation beneath nearly all successful AI development.
Amid the rapid build-out of data centers capable of supporting powerful AI, Nvidia has exploded. Companies like Alphabet and Space Exploration Technologies are pouring billions into AI and data center development, and a big chunk of that spending goes to Nvidia. In fact, on SpaceX's most recent earnings call, CEO Elon Musk said his company would be "exclusive" to Nvidia, because "the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture."
SpaceX also just announced that it has committed funding for the biggest GPU financing deal ever , and since SpaceX is exclusively using Nvidia GPUs, that's where the money is going.
There's been a general tech sell-off over the past week as the market has digested the midterm election results. The S&P 500 , which has become increasingly tech-weighted as its largest components are all tech companies, is down 2.6% since Wednesday, while the even more tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite is down 3.1%. The market anticipates that the incoming Congress could be more hostile to unfettered AI development than the current one, and several incoming governors, among them Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, have already announced that they plan to place moratoriums on data center build-outs in their states until their legislatures act to put more robust protections and regulations in place.
Nvidia, though, has been getting hammered for a completely different reason: CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is now being investigated as an alleged Chinese asset. The company and the FBI are investigating, and it's likely that the stock has not seen its bottom from this development as of this writing.
There are no guarantees about what will happen next, especially because the spy-affair story is both unprecedented for the company and still developing. Meanwhile, Nvidia stock has been dropping like a brick. This isn't simply a case of a tech sell-off that we can expect to be followed by reviving investor confidence as external headwinds ease. But investors can look to history to get a sense of what's likely to come.
Let's look back at Nvidia's history over the past five years -- the period when it became more significant as part of the tech economy. Nvidia fell by at least 20% on five separate occasions over that span, including the current slump. Here's how much it fell each time, and where the stock was 12 months later, or for this year, through today:
In each case, it didn't take too long for the stock to rebound fully and then rise much, much higher. Over the past five years, including all the dips, Nvidia stock has gained more than 500%.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/10/26
Is the current slump any different? It's not likely. Nvidia is still at the center of AI development, and even if there are ramifications for Nvidia due to shifts in the political landscape or issues for Huang himself due to his affair, the company he co-founded still has loads of growth potential.
Right now, Wall Street is expecting that Nvidia will deliver 90% sales growth overall this year and 68% growth next year. It is possible that its revenue growth rate will underperform next year if government impediments to the data center build-out lead hyperscalers, neoclouds, and other tech players to trim back their orders, but Nvidia still makes the AI chips of choice for the biggest data center operators. History is on Nvidia's side, and even if it takes the company more than 12 months to bounce back from this correction, it's likely to happen eventually.

articles.title_orig: Smart ring maker Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
articles.title_zh: Smart ring maker Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
articles.content_orig:
Oura announced on Tuesday that it’s acquiring AI-native primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal comes a few weeks after Oura postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”
Counsel Health is an AI-powered healthcare platform that combines a chat-based medical experience with access to licensed physicians. Its service was integrated into the Oura app in June.
Users can connect with Counsel’s medical AI to get personalized medical advice, and chat with a physician when needed, all within the Oura app. Now, the companies plan to expand on their existing partnership to build across preventative care, acute care, and specialty and chronic care.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By acquiring Counsel Health, Oura is looking to expand its business and help users access medical care.
“Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care, and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale in a press release .
Counsel Health raised a $25 million Series A a year ago, led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and GV. PitchBook estimates it had raised a total of $36 million.
Following the acquisition, Oura says Counsel will continue serving existing and new enterprise partners, with the goal of expanding its AI-native care model to more people beyond Oura’s membership.
Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, alongside the company’s 70 employees, Bloomberg reports.
“At Counsel, we’ve built medical AI around trust, safety and responsibility, keeping physicians in the loop for clinical decisions,” Alagappan said in the press release. “Oura’s data gives clinicians objective context, trended biometrics, and member engagement to deliver more informed care. From the start, our teams bonded over a joint vision, shared culture, and mission, further solidifying as we negotiated our deal over the past few months.”
The deal is expected to close before the end of 2027.
Oura also announced that its revenue grew 153% year-over-year to $533 million for the quarter ended on September 30. For its fiscal year 2026, Oura generated revenue of approximately $1.75 billion, marking 92% year-over-year growth.
The company reached an $11 billion valuation following a $900 million late-stage funding round in October 2025.

articles.title_orig: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
articles.title_zh: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
articles.content_orig:
Three distinct threat activity clusters with shared infrastructure and malware code similarities have been observed targeting telecommunications providers, government organizations, military entities, research institutions, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe over the past year.
Check Point Research is tracking the clusters under the names SilentDelivery , OceanGate , and DarkWire . Although initially assumed to be independent sets of attacks, each with its own backdoors and post-exploitation tooling, they have all been linked through a malware ecosystem called Sparrow.
The entity behind the Sparrow framework has been codenamed CopperDragon , and is assessed to be a digital quartermaster developing tools for China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow , Earth Estries , Tropic Trooper , UAT-9244 , and UAT-8302 .
"Each cluster employed a different toolset and different initial access techniques, including compromising internet-facing infrastructure and highly selective watering hole attacks," Check Point said in a technical report published today. "The compromised websites that were used for watering hole attacks were of government, shipping, and IT and research sectors."
Attacks mounted by FamousSparrow are known for deploying backdoors like SparrowDoor (and its variants Crowdoor and TernDoor ), SparroWocky , and HemiGate . It's also assessed to share some degree of overlap with Salt Typhoon. However, the precise nature of the relationship remains unclear.
The cyber espionage ecosystem linked to CopperDragon is driven by three prominent clusters -
The SilentDelivery chain begins with the attacker injecting heavily obfuscated JavaScript into legitimate websites frequented by their intended targets. Visitors to the sites are greeted by a Google Chrome SSL certificate warning that instructs users to install a "Certificate Fix" utility to restore access.
The so-called utility, once deployed, delivers either SquadC or a SparrowDoor variant. All the compromised websites have been found to be related to government, shipping, IT, and research sectors in the Czech Republic, Germany, France, Taiwan, Nepal, Hong Kong, and Indonesia.
According to a report published by Positive Technologies in August 2026, there are indications that the campaign has also targeted entities in Egypt and the Philippines using this method.
"The JavaScript injected into the compromised websites is heavily obfuscated using jsjiami, a publicly available JavaScript obfuscation service," Check Point said. "It first checks whether the user is running Windows and, in some cases, verifies that the website’s domain matches the intended compromised domain."
The script then repeatedly sends status-check requests to a command-and-control (C2) server to fingerprint the user based on IP and geolocation, and ultimately decide whether to continue the attack and serve the fake warning.
Written in C/C++, SquadC is a Windows backdoor that enables initial foothold over the infected host. It establishes persistence by means of a Windows Registry Run key that masquerades as a Windows update assistant. Further analysis has uncovered that the malware is also distributed via phishing emails targeting Indonesian organizations.
The phishing email comes with a Windows Shortcut (LNK) disguised as a PDF document, which, when opened, abuses the legitimate "ftp.exe" binary to run a batch script that's responsible for displaying an empty file as a decoy, while launching SquadC via DLL sideloading.
The OceanGate operation, on the other hand, has been observed targeting both Windows and Linux environments, deploying previously undocumented tooling to maintain access, move laterally across the network, and exfiltrate sensitive data.
The Linux phase of the attack involves two new backdoors -
"After harvesting credentials from multiple users and establishing a strong foothold in the Linux environment, the actor moved into the Windows environment," Check Point explained. "The actor attempted to log in to several Windows machines over RDP, trying different passwords until it successfully authenticated with an administrator account."
This step is followed by the deployment of bespoke post-exploitation tools and a variant of SparrowDoor -
What's more, the threat actor has been found incorporating kernel rootkits and kernel-level access capabilities into SparrowDoor and SparrowShell to evade defenses through process hiding and to capture and manipulate network packet capture using WinDivert drivers.
"The actor abused the driver to convert SparrowDoor into a passive backdoor that intercepts and manipulates packets at the kernel level, making its traffic less visible," Check Point said. "This allows the backdoor to listen internally on one port while receiving connections through an externally accessible port, such as 443, that is already used by a legitimate service."
"The backdoor applies a strict filter to intercept connections from a specific source IP address to the legitimate service's port. It manipulates the packet and rewrites the destination port to the backdoor’s internal listening port, typically a high port such as 49628. For response traffic, it rewrites the source port back to the external service port, making the responses appear to originate from the legitimate service."
Interestingly, SparrowShell shares code- and infrastructure-level similarities with a malware called Mélofée that was first described by ExaTrack in March 2023 as based on the open-source Reptile rootkit. This has raised the possibility that CopperDragon is also behind the development and supply of Mélofée.
The third and last cluster of activity centers around Latin America, with a particular focus on telecommunications operators and government entities. These attacks led to the deployment of two newly identified backdoors called CopperDoor and CopperDNS as a possible replacement for SparrowDoor.
Also supporting these operations is a set of custom tools -
"The operation heavily relies on DLL sideloading as a primary execution technique, often abusing executables that are not widely observed among other threat actors in the wild," Check Point said. "To minimize their footprint, the operators deliberately avoided creating new directories on disk, instead placing their tools within existing system paths."
"CopperDoor infrastructure demonstrated a higher level of operational security. Most IP addresses were located in Latin America, often within the same country as the victim organization. This proximity likely helps the malicious traffic blend in with legitimate network activity and reduces the chances of detection."

articles.title_orig: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Stocks fell on Tuesday after October inflation data came in hotter than expected and a key Federal Reserve official hinted at the possibility of a half-point rise in rates next month.
The S&P 500 traded down 0.6%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 181 points, or 0.3%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.1%.
Nvidia dragged down the three major averages, falling 6%. The stock sat out Monday's tech-fueled rally following CEO Jensen Huang's admission over the weekend to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy .
The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the gain of 0.3% that economists polled by Dow Jones expected. Core CPI — which excludes volatile food and energy costs — increased 0.3% in October, whereas economists had called for a 0.2% advance. Annual figures were not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown.
Treasury yields jumped as traders reacted to the report, fearing that interest rate increases could now be more likely in 2027. The 10-year Treasury note yield in particular advanced back above 5% .
Earlier Tuesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech in London that he thinks a December rate hike is likely and opened the door for a possible half-point increase amid persistent  inflationary pressures.
"While the precise timing of the hikes doesn't matter, ensuring that the promised hikes are implemented in a reasonable period of time does," he said.
Traders now see a December rate hike as a near certainty and a small chance of a supersized increase. They also expect at least a quarter-point hike at some point next year.
"There's an extrapolation that maybe the Fed's going to have to hike rates more aggressively next year," said Tom Hainlin, national investment strategist at U.S. Bank Asset Management. He later added, "The CPI print said perhaps inflation is going to be a little stickier for a little longer."
Tuesday's retreat came one day after the S&P 500 posted its best day since April. The push and pull come after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned about the potential for a slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
Citi upgraded the tokenization stock Securitize while maintaining its $14 price target on the shares, following the company's third quarter earnings Monday evening and announced expansion into asset-backed finance.
Shares were up nearly 20% in afternoon trading.
"Management 3Q commentary provided greater visibility into SECZ's monetization opportunity across token issuance, servicing, trading, stablecoin infrastructure, and credit origination through the pending River One acquisition," Citi analyst Peter Christiansen said in a note Tuesday. "Although we lower near-term profitability expectations following higher-than-expected nonrecurring operating expenses, we come away from the quarter with greater conviction that SECZ is expanding its role across multiple layers of the tokenization value chain … The valuation has become more attractive, supporting our upgrade to Buy/HR."
For more on Securitize's earnings, read our story and watch our exclusive interview with CEO Carlos Domingo here .
The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July , reaching $3.978 a gallon on Tuesday.
Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and 39 cents from a month ago, according to AAA . Lower crude prices and normal autumn seasonality have contributed to the decline.
Brent briefly fell below $90 a barrel in hopes of easing U.S.-Iran tensions and recovering oil flows around the Strait of Hormuz.
The Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, however, warned Tuesday that earlier energy shocks may continue affecting prices into 2027.
"While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained," he said.
Although further interest-rate increases could pressure bond prices in the near term, Wells Fargo strategists believe today's higher yields offer more income and a stronger starting point for long-term returns.
The firm examined five-, seven- and 10-year periods and found that the relationship between starting yields and subsequent annualized returns was strongest over approximately seven years. Higher income may also help cushion bond-price declines when market rates rise.
"Investors do not need to wait for the peak in interest rates to find opportunities in fixed income," wrote Luis Alvarado, co-head of global fixed-income strategy at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
Wells Fargo favors short- and intermediate-term bonds, which offer attractive income without the greater interest-rate sensitivity of longer maturities. High-quality bonds may also provide diversification, reduce portfolio volatility and support cash-flow planning.
Separately, the firm remains neutral on information technology following the October sell-off while favoring communication services, industrials and materials as broader beneficiaries of AI investment.
Check out CNBC's live blog to read more about the stocks making midday moves here .
— John Melloy, Deena Zaidi and Darla Mercado
Nike is hosting its first Investor Day since 2017 next week under a new management team led by CEO Elliott Hill.
The event could serve as a crucial moment for the company that has been struggling to turn its business around.
"Next week will be an opportunity for management to signal the pathway ahead for Nike's medium-term growth story," Bernstein analyst Aneesha Sherman wrote in a Tuesday research note.
Investors are weighing up when the sportswear's business will stabilize from stagnating sales and lack of product innovation.
In the foreseeable future, analysts estimate Nike's five-year sales growth "will likely be flattish."
Bernstein sees Fiscal year 2027 as a "reset" in the Lifestyle category modeling a mid-teens decline, while Nike's other core segment, Performance grows 10%.
While the event itself may not be a catalyst for the stock which has gained 12% over the last month, Bernstein said it could "drive incremental investor confidence of a multi-year recovery."
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note jumped on Tuesday, moving back above the key 5% level, after hotter-than-expected inflation data .
The yield climbed more than 14 basis points to 5.004%. It last traded above the 5% level earlier this month. Read more .
Dallas Federal Reserve President Lorie Logan said Tuesday that she expects two more interest rate hikes will be needed as the central bank struggles to bring inflation lower.
"Tighter policy will be necessary to appropriately balance the outlook and risks for inflation and employment. And it is important to achieve that balance promptly," the policymaker said during an energy conference in Houston. "The longer above-target inflation persists, the greater the risk that it becomes baked into behavior."
Earlier in the day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he expects a quarter percentage point hike would be appropriate at the next policy meeting in December. He even raised the notion that the Fed may have to raise by half a point should inflation numbers come in higher than expected, as they did in Tuesday's consumer price index report.
However, Logan said she thinks two more quarter-point moves would be appropriate before the Fed could take a break.
"The exact pace of increases could depend on the near-term economic and financial environment," she said. "After two more increases are in place, it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate. The goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive so we can sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices."
Logan is a voter this year on the rate-setting Federal Open Market

articles.title_orig: China calls for stronger dialogue, cooperation with France
articles.title_zh: China calls for stronger dialogue, cooperation with France
articles.content_orig:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Tuesday called for stronger dialogue and cooperation with France to deepen political mutual trust and jointly address global risks and challenges, state media reported.
During a telephone conversation with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, Wang said Beijing was ready to work with Paris to fulfill their responsibilities as permanent members of the UN Security Council.
The two countries should also work together to safeguard the common interests of the international community, Wang said, according to state-run Xinhua News Agency.
He expressed hope that France would "honor its commitment to the 'one-China principle' through concrete actions and safeguard the political foundation of China-France relations."
Wang also urged the EU to work with China to establish "stable and balanced" trade relations, emphasizing their importance as major trading partners.
The two sides "stand to gain from cooperation and lose from confrontation," he said.
Barrot, for his part, said France attached great importance to China's status as a major country and remained committed to the one-China policy, according to Xinhua.
He added that Paris was ready to play an active role in promoting dialogue and cooperation between the EU and China.
The two ministers also exchanged views on issues of mutual concern, including the election of the UN secretary-general.
Separately, Wang held talks with Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar in Beijing on Tuesday.
Wang said China was ready to work with Slovakia to advance a vision of global governance based on extensive consultation, joint contributions and shared benefits.
He also called for jointly building a community with a shared future for humanity, according to Xinhua.
Blanar reaffirmed Slovakia's commitment to the one-China policy and described Beijing as an important partner.
He said Slovakia would continue working to provide a stable and favorable environment for Chinese companies to invest and cooperate in the country.

articles.title_orig: Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
articles.title_zh: Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
articles.content_orig:
Google Fi will swap users between two 5G networks, but only if your phone is a Pixel 9 or newer.﻿
Google Fi will swap users between two 5G networks, but only if your phone is a Pixel 9 or newer.﻿
Google Fi is launching a new “super network” that can automatically switch users between two different 5G networks depending on which one has better connectivity. The feature is rolling out starting today on Pixel 9 and newer phones that have Google Fi active on eSIM and have any non-Fi SIMs disabled.
When Google Fi first launched in 2015, users were originally able to switch between T-Mobile and Sprint’s networks. But those two networks eventually became one when T-Mobile acquired Sprint in 2020, and so the network switching stopped there. Jane Harnett, Google Fi Wireless senior product manager, told The Verge that Fi stopped offering the feature because “the wireless landscape consolidated via mergers and limited our ability to offer multiple networks within the US.” (Networking switching has continued to be available internationally .)
Now the feature is returning to the US, with Fi once again hopping between two networks. Harnett declined to share which networks Fi will be working with to make this happen. Google Fi’s FAQs say it currently provides coverage through T-Mobile’s network.
According to Harnett, Google Fi’s new approach to network switching is faster than what it offered before, and uses eSIMs’ ability to connect to multiple carriers at once :
“Previously Fi’s switching was single-SIM switching which could only connect to one network at a time, so your phone had to wait until service dropped completely before performing a slow SIM profile swap into another network without knowing if coverage was actually better there. Fi also tried dual-SIM iterations that required both a physical SIM and eSIM which could be slower to transition.
Now we are back with added networks domestically. We have rebuilt the experience from the ground up for the modern era. With our new switching on newer Pixel devices, your phone keeps two eSIM network profiles on standby at the same time (via MEP technology) and uses the Android OS to monitor live connection quality. It also lets your phone transition faster and more fluidly with minimal battery impact—knowing a better connection is available before it switches.”

articles.title_orig: Michael Bloomberg and Diana Taylor Get Married After 26 Years
articles.title_zh: Michael Bloomberg and Diana Taylor Get Married After 26 Years
articles.content_orig:
Things you buy through our links may earn Vox Media a commission
Sometimes it takes a quarter-century, but he will be down to DTR. A spokesperson for former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg announced on Monday that he and his longtime partner, Diana Taylor, have married after 26 years together. It was “a small, private ceremony at their home on the Upper East Side,” and Bloomberg’s daughters from his first marriage, Emma and Georgina, were there alongside other family members.
Bloomberg and Taylor met in 2000, when he was first running for mayor. They were seated next to each other by chance at the notoriously romantic Citizens Budget Commission meeting. Thankfully, fate struck a second time when they were dining at the same restaurant later that night. In Taylor’s telling , Bloomberg saw her, approached her table, and asked her to have a drink afterward.
Bloomberg, who’s 84, served as the city’s mayor for three consecutive terms from 2002 to 2013. During his tenure, Taylor, a 71-year-old business executive who was married once before she met Bloomberg, served as the city’s unofficial First Lady. (She was also the New York superintendent of banks from 2003 to 2007.) Taylor has described herself as a “step-whatever” to Bloomberg’s children.
Why now? In 2020, when Bloomberg was running for president, Gayle King asked about his relationship with Taylor and whether he planned to be the first modern-day unmarried president. “We’ve only been living together for 19 years and, I think it’s fair if I can speak for her as well, neither of us have any plans to change,” he replied coyly. Their domestic partnership came up a few times during his presidential run — in her own interview with the Washington Post , Taylor said she hates the term girlfriend “because it sounds so temporary” and “junior high” but finds partner too business-y. “Nobody’s come up with language around what we are,” she said.
Well, now we can officially call them man and wife. Could death and taxes have brought them to the altar? Or as one X user theorized , maybe it took two decades to lock in their prenup? Whatever it is, good for them. It really is never too late to get hitched.
